title: About Agra Orthopaedic Society
summary: A professional home for orthopaedic learning, ethical practice, fellowship, and public service in Agra since 1979.

sections.title: A society built around shared learning
paragraphs: Agra Orthopaedic Society brings orthopaedic surgeons and trainees together through academic meetings, continuing medical education, skills development, research, professional fellowship, and community awareness.
The society connects local clinical experience with wider academic collaboration while preserving the professional legacy built by generations of orthopaedic surgeons in Agra.

sections.title: What guides the society
bullets: Advance orthopaedic knowledge through regular academic activity.
Encourage ethical, evidence-informed, and compassionate patient care.
Support postgraduate education, presentation, research, and mentorship.
Contribute to public understanding of bone, joint, injury, and mobility health.
Strengthen fellowship and collaboration across the orthopaedic community.

title: Membership
summary: Join a professional community centred on learning, fellowship, ethics, and service.

sections.title: For orthopaedic professionals in and around Agra
paragraphs: AOS membership is intended for orthopaedic surgeons, postgraduate trainees, and professionals connected with the society’s academic and ethical objectives.
For current eligibility, fee details, and document requirements, contact the society office. Applications remain subject to verification and approval under AOS rules.

sections.title: What membership supports
bullets: Academic meetings, CME programmes, and workshops.
Postgraduate presentation and mentorship opportunities.
Professional fellowship across institutions and generations.
Public-awareness and community-facing orthopaedic initiatives.

sections.title: AOS Digital Directory 2026–2027
paragraphs: AOS is updating its official member records through a consent-led digital directory. Directory submissions support member communication, academic activity, society records, and an accurate professional network for the current term.

The directory is intended for circulation among AOS members. It will not be published as an open website directory until secure member access and the society’s final verification process are in place.

sections.title: Members stay in control
bullets: Each member chooses which professional details may appear in the directory.
Photograph permission is recorded separately from general directory consent.
Family details and family photographs remain limited to internal family or social communication where permission was given.
Members may contact the society office to correct or update their official record.

title: Public Awareness
summary: Clear, responsible starting points for bone, joint, injury, and mobility health.

sections.title: Health information, not a diagnosis
paragraphs: Good bone and joint health begins with regular movement, appropriate strength work, balanced nutrition, injury prevention, and timely assessment when symptoms persist.
General information cannot replace examination or individual medical advice. For urgent injury, severe pain, weakness, numbness, deformity, or loss of function, seek qualified medical care promptly.

sections.title: AOS Bone & Joint Week 2026
paragraphs: AOS is observing Bone & Joint Week from 2 August to 9 August 2026 under the IOA/UPOA public-awareness theme: One week, one activity, one community impact.

The campaign is being carried forward locally as Agra Moves Better - 2026, with practical public-awareness and preventive-health activities for safer movement, stronger bones and healthier communities.
bullets: 1 August 2026: Agra Moves Better launch and Media, NGO & Founding Partners' Meet.
2 August 2026: Police Wellness & Family Health Camp at Police Lines, Agra.
3 August 2026: Media-awareness and hospital-based BMD screening record.
4 August 2026: National Bone & Joint Day Police Workplace Ergonomics and CPR awareness programme at Police Lines, Agra.
6 August 2026: Community bone-health screening and awareness outreach with local women’s and service organisations.
7 August 2026: Akashvani radio awareness and G.L. Public School posture/movement outreach.
Campaign themes include osteoporosis, joint pain, posture, exercise, fall prevention, road and workplace injury prevention, and healthy ageing.

sections.title: Agra Moves Better - 2026
paragraphs: Agra Moves Better - 2026 was formally launched on 1 August 2026 with a Media, NGO and Founding Partners' Meet at Lemon Tree Hotel, Khandari, Agra.

The campaign invites city institutions, social organisations, schools, workplaces, healthcare teams and volunteers to participate in a shared action plan for better bone, joint, muscle and spine health.
bullets: Campaign message: Better Bones, Better Life, Better Agra.
Launch outcome: a shared city action plan for safer movement, stronger bones and healthier communities.
AOS leadership: Dr Atul Kulshreshtha, President; Dr Sanjay Chaturvedi, Secretary; Dr D. V. Sharma, Chairman, Agra Moves Better - 2026.
Selected launch photographs — /gallery/#agra-moves-better-august-2026
Public-awareness PDFs — /downloads-notices/
Campaign media and activity dossiers — /downloads-notices/

sections.title: Police Wellness & Family Health Camp
paragraphs: On 2 August 2026, AOS organised a Police Wellness & Family Health Camp at the Police Training Centre, Police Lines, Agra, in association with Agra Police, VAMA Saarthi and Police Hospital.

The activity brought preventive orthopaedic and neurological screening to police personnel and their families, with report review and counselling on posture, exercise, nutrition, sunlight exposure and safe screen use.
bullets: Approximately 200 people were reached.
100 BMD tests and 60 Vitamin-D tests were recorded in the activity dossier.
Clinical services included BMD screening, selected Vitamin-D testing, neurological assessment, orthopaedic consultation and individual counselling.
Photographs from the camp are available in the gallery — /gallery/#police-wellness-august-2026

sections.title: Media Awareness & BMD Screening Record
paragraphs: On 3 August 2026, the Agra Moves Better record combined public-health messaging through supplied Hindi print-media coverage with preventive bone-health screening through two BMD machines deployed at multiple hospitals in Agra.
The public message connected road-safety trauma prevention, police occupational musculoskeletal health and early joint-care with timely assessment and safer daily movement.
bullets: Three supplied print clippings carried AOS-linked prevention messages on road trauma, police ergonomics and early knee, bone and muscle health.
Two BMD machines were recorded as deployed for hospital-based screening across multiple hospitals.
The campaign messages included safer roads, timely response, CPR awareness, duty ergonomics, posture, stretching, early joint-care and healthy movement.
Figures quoted in the dossier are reproduced from supplied press coverage and external study references; they are not presented as results of an AOS screening cohort.
Daily Activity & Media Dossier, 3 August 2026 — /downloads-notices/

sections.title: National Bone & Joint Day: Fit Police, Strong Spine
paragraphs: On 4 August 2026, AOS continued Agra Moves Better - 2026 with a Police Workplace Ergonomics and CPR awareness programme at Prashant Memorial Hall, Police Lines, Agra.

The programme focused on practical duty-related prevention: posture during standing, patrolling, driving and desk work, safe lifting, duty-break stretching, and early attention to neck, back, shoulder and knee pain.
bullets: Programme message: Fit Police, strong spine, better service.
Activity focus: CPR awareness, Police Workplace Ergonomics, safe movement and injury prevention.
Campaign context: National Bone & Joint Day under Agra Moves Better - 2026.
Photographs from the programme are available in the gallery — /gallery/#police-ergonomics-august-2026

sections.title: Community Bone-Health Screening & Awareness Outreach
paragraphs: On 6 August 2026, AOS continued Agra Moves Better - 2026 through community-based bone-health screening, counselling and practical awareness with Shri Maheshwari Mahila Mandal, Lions Club Sparkle Surbhi and Inner Wheel Club of Agra Midtown.

The activity model combined BMD screening with explanation, fall-prevention messages, posture awareness and counselling, so screening could lead to safer movement and appropriate follow-up rather than remaining a stand-alone test.
bullets: 58 BMD screening registrations were documented in the privacy-safe activity summary.
The outreach used public campaign material on strong bones, posture, safe movement and fall prevention.
Patient-identifying register photographs are retained only as supporting evidence and are not reproduced on the public website.
Selected photographs from the outreach are available in the gallery — /gallery/#community-bone-health-august-2026
6 August Activity Dossier — /downloads-notices/

sections.title: Akashvani Radio & School Outreach
paragraphs: On 7 August 2026, AOS extended Agra Moves Better - 2026 through mass communication and school engagement: an Akashvani radio interaction for city-wide public awareness and an in-person school programme at G.L. Public School.

The common message was that many future bone, joint, muscle and spine problems can be reduced by correct movement and posture, regular physical activity, sensible screen habits, safe school-bag use and balanced nutrition.
bullets: Akashvani Varta carried AOS messages on sitting, standing, walking, sleeping, exercise, nutrition, tobacco/alcohol avoidance, posture and osteoporosis awareness.
The G.L. Public School programme focused on healthy students, healthy spine, correct study posture, movement breaks, sports, screen habits and safe bag handling.
The programme reached both general listeners and school-age children with the same prevention-first message.
7 August Activity Dossier — /downloads-notices/

sections.title: Daily Hindi public-awareness posts
paragraphs: AOS will use its Facebook page for regular Hindi public-awareness posts on common orthopaedic problems. The aim is to share one clear, practical topic at a time for patients and families in Agra.

Suggested themes include osteoporosis, knee arthritis, back pain, fracture first aid, sports injury prevention, senior-citizen falls, road-safety trauma prevention, posture, safe exercise, and when to seek urgent orthopaedic care.
bullets: Monday: knee pain and osteoarthritis
Wednesday: shoulder myth-buster
Friday: practical self-care, cramps, stretching, fall prevention, or posture
Sunday: simple patient question or doctor’s note
